To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the MAC protocols can be classified into three categories: (i) contention-based, (ii) time-based, and (iii) preamble sampling MAC protocols; (iii) preamble-based MAC protocols are the best choice when the traffic load is low and the energy consumption is a major concern.
the most important MAC protocol categories in the field of WSNs are contention-based, contention-free, TDMA, and preamble sampling.

preamble sampling MAC protocols are an interesting option to be considered when designing a WSN, especially if a very large number of sensors are involved and/or if the network is expected to have a very low load.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of MAC protocols designed specifically for WSNs.
the design of MAC protocols for WSNs with low energy consumption at very low loads, with special attention to preamble sampling protocols.
providing a survey of the most important and recent MAC protocols designed for the WSN domain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the preamble sampling technique is a good choice when the network is not very dense and the traffic is light.

the most suitable category of MAC protocols for WSNs applications is the preamble sampling one, since it provides extremely low energy consumption and a simple operation, and is also suitable for a wide range of application scenarios.
preamble sampling MAC protocols are an excellent choice when low energy operation is a requirement in a WSN, as long as the traffic conditions allow the use of these protocols.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MAC protocols designed for low energy operation in WNSs are classified into three categories: contention-based, preamble sampling and TDMA-based.
preamble sampling MAC protocols are an excellent choice when the network is not very dense and when a high level of energy efficiency is needed.
, for a given application, the most suitable MAC category is the one with the lowest energy consumption for the given application load, while maintaining the required QoS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design of MAC protocols for WSNs has reached maturity and that the most relevant MAC protocol categories are already defined.
preamble sampling techniques are a very good option for applications with low traffic loads, where the energy efficiency is a key design requirement.
the MAC protocols designed for the different types of WSNs are very diverse, which is a consequence of the different application constraints.
